plan: To preserve capital, sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU, MSFU, PLTU) to zero.
Trim QQQI to 20% to meet the single name concentration limit.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation and reduces overall portfolio risk.
It aims for a steady, low-drawdown approach by removing high-beta and leveraged positions.
conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for a realistic ~0.5-1.5%/month return, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and lowering concentration. Expect lower volatility but also limited upside potential.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU, MSFU, PLTU) to small allocations to reduce overall leverage.
Trim QQQI to 25% to comply with the single name concentration limit.
Buy ERX at 4% as a new position, leveraging a strong scanner long setup.
This plan balances risk and growth, maintaining some tech exposure while reducing overall portfolio risk.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets a realistic ~1.5-2.5%/month return, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces leverage and concentration while adding a high-quality scanner setup. Expect moderate volatility and growth potential.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to meet the single name concentration limit.
Add to existing leveraged ETFs (METU, SOXL, MUU, MSFU, PLTU, SPAL) to increase exposure to high-beta sectors.
Buy ERX at 6% as a new position, leveraging a strong scanner long setup.
This plan aims for aggressive growth by concentrating in leveraged ETFs and high-scoring setups, accepting higher risk.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets a realistic ~3-4%/month return, aiming for stretched growth. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and high-beta names. Be aware of substantially higher drawdown risk and the daily decay/rebalancing of leveraged ETFs.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, MUU, SPAL) and high-beta single names (METU, MSFU, PLTU) to zero.
Add to QQQI, increasing its allocation to 30% to prioritize income generation.
This plan focuses on rotating into income-generating ETFs for steady distributions.
It aims for low drawdown and reliable income over growth, acting as a cash-like position.
income.read: This income plan targets a realistic ~0.5-1.0%/month return, prioritizing yield and low drawdown. It significantly reduces growth-oriented and leveraged positions. While aiming for steady distributions, remember that NAV can still fall, and distributions are variable.
